chunks: From him, from Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Wassash, who said:

I asked Al-Rida (peace be upon him): 'Is it permissible to sell the palm trees when they have borne fruit?' He said: 'It is not permissible to sell them until they become ripe (yazhwa).' I said: 'And what is ripening (al-zahw)? May I be your ransom.' He said: 'They turn red and yellow, and similar to that.'

key_terms.يَزْهُوَ: to become ripe or mature (specifically regarding fruit)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the validity of selling fruit on trees in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Al-Rida (AS) clarifies the condition of *zahw* (ripening) for the permissibility of selling fruit on the tree, specifying that mere bearing of fruit is insufficient. He defines *zahw* as the visible change in color, such as turning red or yellow, which ensures the buyer knows exactly what they are purchasing, thereby preventing *gharar* (uncertainty). This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on clarity and fairness in commercial transactions to avoid disputes over quality and quantity.
